name: Kahului International Airport
before:
Maui's main airport, just east of Kahului, and in full operation since 1952.

Most arrivals come from Honolulu. The Honolulu to Kahului corridor is one of the heaviest trafficked air routes in the United States, ranked thirteenth in 2004 with 1,632,000 passengers.

The gate layout is worth knowing because it is not intuitive. Odd numbered gates have jetways and even numbered ones use stairs down to the ramp. The south side holds gates 1 to 16 and the north side gates 17 to 39. Inter-island flights use one set of gates and overseas flights another, because the larger transoceanic aircraft will not fit at every stand. Four gates are rarely used at all for that reason.

Mainland non-stop flights began in 1982 and 1983, and today the airport takes A330s, 767s and 777s alongside the 717s and 737s that work the inter-island routes.

USDA agricultural inspection sits on the ground level alongside ticketing and baggage claim.

The code OGG honours Bertram Hogg, a Kauai born pilot who flew for what is now Hawaiian Airlines.
after:
Maui's main airport, just east of Kahului. It has been in full operation since 1952 and is the second busiest airport in Hawaii, after Honolulu. The FAA's preliminary figures show nearly 3.5 million passengers boarding flights here in 2025.

Scheduled flights from the mainland began in 1983. Hawaiian Airlines flies Boeing 717s between the islands, and from 3 October 2026 Alaska Airlines adds three daily Boeing 737-800 round trips to Honolulu.

Travellers flying on to the US mainland must have their bags inspected by the US Department of Agriculture, at stations in front of or at the airline check-in counters.

The code OGG honours Jim Hogg, a former Hawaiian Airlines pilot.

claims.note: The FAA's CY2025 table has no row at all for Maui's two other airports, Kapalua and Hana; the other Maui County airports in it (Molokai, Lanai) are on other islands.
